runs.file: 2026-10-16 Run - LZRFY Localiza Rent a Car.md
runs.entry: Price **BRL 49.69** (RENT3 close of 2026-10-16, Yahoo Finance chart API, aggregator, flagged; RENT4 BRL 48.20; LZRFY US$9.80 not used; one ADR one share). Shares **1,104,614,922** at 2026-06-30 (ITR 2Q26 note 21: 1,064,036,631 common and 40,578,291 transitional preferred RENT4 outstanding, both counted as one class, a CONVENTION of the run; no later notice to the market changes the count); cap **BRL 54,828M**. Sovereign **12.87%** (Tesouro Nacional, the longest nominal bond it publishes, maturing 2037, base date 2026-10-15; no BRL row in the protocol's table). Not an SEC registrant (Localiza Franchising S.A., CIK 0001051966, deregistered 2005, not the subject); `tools/run.py` and `Screens/cover_shares.py` returned nothing and all arithmetic was done by hand from the statements. Documents read: the DFP FY2025 filed with the CVM 2026-02-26 (sequence 154953) with the management report; the ITR 2Q26; the Reference Form 2026 v5; releases 4Q25 and 2Q26; ten years of DFPs from the CVM open data. Cross-check: FY2025 EBIT BRL 7,811.6M in three places. The brief departed in one stated place: the lines of evidence chosen by the analyst from the management report and notes. Corporate events since 2017 found by the analyst: offerings of BRL 1.8B (2019) and BRL 4.5B (June 2023); the all-share merger with Locamerica effective 2022-07-01, the CADE carve-out of about 49,000 cars sold to a Brookfield fund (now Unidas Locadora) for BRL 3,878.9M; the brand Localiza&Co, legal name unchanged; Locamerica merged into the company 2025-08-01; the RENT4 bonus issue of 2025-12-29; the Voll stake sold January 2026 for BRL 382.0M; no split. **Q1 IN**: a Brazilian car renter (Car Rental and Fleet Rental segments, Seminovos reselling the decommissioned cars through 263 own stores), the key variables (rate per day and utilization, depreciation per car as purchase less resale, funding cost floating over the CDI) reported every year. **Q2 OUT**: Car Rental, 54.3% of FY2021 to FY2025 segment EBIT, decides, and has a standing castle that protects only ordinary returns: the scale leader (44.5% of car rental by fleet, 286,347 cars bought in 2025 against about 110,000 for its 'main direct competitor') and the low-cost buyer and reseller, yet pre-tax EBIT on average capital employed 15.6% mean FY2016 to FY2025 (16.7% without goodwill), about 10.3% after 34% tax against a long NTN-F averaging 10.8% in the same years; Movida 14.0%, Locamerica 13.9% (FY2018 to FY2024), Unidas Locadora 9.4% (FY2024 to FY2025); the edge small over the span and absent after the merger; ROE 15% to 27% before 2022 with net debt about equal to equity, about 7% to 9% after; rates repriced only after depreciation per car rose from BRL 941 (2021) to BRL 10,109 (2024); the price of a rental day fallen from 35% to about 10% of the minimum wage since 2003; the filings name no rival, Movida, Locamerica and Unidas Locadora read as a CONVENTION of the run, the unnamed global brands flagged. Q3 to Q12 not reached. Facts after the stop: capital employed BRL 3.6B (FY2015) to BRL 58.5B (FY2025), BRL 8.4B of it merger goodwill; added capital FY2021 to FY2025 earning about 7.6% after tax; residual-value revisions in 2Q23, 2Q24 and 3Q25; loans and debentures BRL 44.6B at 2026-06-30, net debt BRL 32,352M, pre-tax earnings over interest 1.69 times (FY2025); a net deferred tax liability of BRL 2.0B from accelerated tax depreciation. **Integrity facts recorded, not judged**: a featured adjusted net income of BRL 3.4B against filed BRL 1,870.4M, adding back a residual-value revision called non-recurring for the third year running; an executive pay metric (ROIC spread) that leaves the merger goodwill out of invested capital; a restricted-share plan for senior managers the filer says is 'not considered part of the Company's compensation strategy' and leaves out of the pay chart; buybacks in 2024 at about BRL 40 to 42.5 with no stated price, partly to settle incentive plans. Owner cash FY2021 to FY2025 (FY2021 and FY2022 on the company's own pro forma combined with Locamerica), all-equity after 34% tax less the interest-on-equity deduction, car depreciation as the maintenance guess: BRL 4,186M a year; equity-only BRL 1,419M. COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE: value **BRL -9.92 to BRL 0.16** a share at 12.87% (the growth case the bottom, bought growth earning below the discount rate; no-growth the top) against BRL 49.69; best case 4.8% on the whole business, no case earns the floor; literal 12.9% growth beside, BRL -18.60; fair **BRL 5.81 all-equity** (BRL 11.90 equity-only), above the top of the range because the ten percent floor is below the BRL sovereign; not armed, the box being OUT at Q2. Contrary evidence tested: 1H26 annualized at cash tax reaches about 10.4%, one half-year, not credited. Contamination declared by the analyst: one filtered `Test Runs/` listing showing an AMH run name and a SUNB run name, the TRN commit subjects, research-folder names in git status, the memory index and `.gitignore` comments naming other runs; none opened or used. Commits b1337c35 (template), b9d45570 (Step 0, foundations, standing rule, Q1), ec4d75a4 (Q2), be06bb31 (close). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_ids.py` 58 ids, no problem; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_check.py` 24 quoted fragments, 24 matched, no slip, no missing id, no E-id. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) the ten percent floor sits below this currency's long government bond (12.87%), so Part VII's fair price lands above the top of the value range, and the text has no rule for a currency whose bond exceeds the floor; (2) Q2's ordinary-returns test names no yardstick (rivals, cost of debt or sovereign); (3) under IFRS a fleet business's car purchases and sales run through operating cash, so the template's capital spending does not find them; (4) the Whose-tax convention is silent on a deferral from accelerated depreciation that reverses only when the fleet stops growing; (5) the template has no line for a filer that names no rival; (6) the per-share figure with a transitional second share class. Could not get: the total stock-pay expense; an audited combined statement for FY2021 and FY2022 (pro forma used); a re-read of the 2017 Hertz Brasil deal; any filing from the unnamed global brands.
runs.narr: OUT at Q2 after Q1 IN (a Brazilian car renter and fleet lessor that resells its own cars, merged with Locamerica in 2022). Car Rental, 54.3% of FY2021 to FY2025 segment EBIT, decides: a standing castle that protects only ordinary returns; the scale leader and low-cost buyer and reseller of cars (44.5% of car rental by fleet), yet pre-tax EBIT on capital employed 15.6% mean FY2016 to FY2025, about 10.3% after tax against a long NTN-F of 10.8% in the same years, Movida 14.0%, Locamerica 13.9%, Unidas Locadora 9.4% (rivals a CONVENTION of the run), the edge small and absent after the merger, ROE made by leverage before 2022 and about 7% since. Facts after the stop: capital employed from BRL 3.6B to BRL 58.5B, added capital earning about 7.6% after tax, three residual-value revisions 2023 to 2025, net debt BRL 32.4B, coverage 1.69 times; integrity facts recorded, not judged: an adjusted net income adding back a recurring 'non-recurring' write-down, a pay metric leaving out the merger goodwill, a restricted-share plan kept out of the pay chart, unpriced buybacks. COMPUTATION beneath the stop: value BRL -9.92 to BRL 0.16 at 12.87% against BRL 49.69, no case earning the floor; fair BRL 5.81 all-equity, BRL 11.90 equity-only, not armed. Framework gaps for the operator: a floor below the currency's sovereign, no yardstick for ordinary returns, fleet purchases inside IFRS operating cash, accelerated-depreciation deferrals under Whose tax, a filer naming no rival, a transitional share class.
